Hannah — quick technical clarifications for the egress & KMS note:
- Data residency: we maintain tenant isolation and can pin workloads to a single region; persistent storage uses encrypted S3 buckets with region scoping.
- Egress controls: default behavior is to restrict outbound connections to customer-approved endpoints; we support network ACLs and VPC endpoints. We also provide an "egress allowlist" configuration and an S3 VPC endpoint option to prevent public S3 egress.
- KMS: support for customer-provided CMKs (AWS KMS) is available. We will include the kms-integration-diagram.png and a short FAQ about rotation/rotation policy.
- Audit logs: CloudTrail and app-level audit events are exportable — we’ll include how to configure delivery to a customer-owned S3 bucket.

I'll attach the pen-test attestation and the egress-control policy draft for review.

Maria — answering your two points:
1) Backups/snapshots: Redwood’s default configuration keeps backups in the same region as the primary dataset. Cross-region replication is opt-in and requires explicit configuration and customer consent. We’ll include a short backup-residency statement document.
2) BYOK revocation: if a customer revokes a CMK, access to data encrypted with that key will be blocked unless the customer provides a new key and re-encrypts or grants a decryption path. We document key rotation and emergency recovery options in the runbook; we note that key management is ultimately the customer’s responsibility for BYOK.
